claims.text: Incorporating 5 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles into CoCrFeNi will produce a stable, continuous CaF2-rich tribofilm during sliding.
The CaF2-rich tribofilm will reduce interfacial shear.
The CaF2-rich tribofilm will reduce oxide formation.
Mechanical alloying will uniformly disperse 5 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
CaF2 has sufficiently low shear strength to provide an in-situ lubricious layer.
The CaF2 layer will resist high-temperature oxidation.
The CaF2 layer will maintain a lubricious interface throughout 25–800 °C.
At each of 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C, the CaF2-modified alloy will have at least 30% lower steady-state coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
At each of 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C, the CaF2-modified alloy will have at least 50% lower specific wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The claimed friction and wear improvements will persist under normal loads from 5 to 20 N in ambient air at approximately 20% relative humidity and a sliding speed of 10 cm/s.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.6 at 25 °C.
The coefficient of friction of unmodified CoCrFeNi rises to approximately 0.8 at 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has a specific wear rate of approximately 1×10^-5 mm^3/Nm.
CaF2 grain coarsening or segregation may occur at the highest test temperatures and impair performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that both thresholds are met across the full set of temperatures, so failure at even one temperature contradicts that universal prediction. The falsification rule instead requires failure at three or more temperatures.
Performance is claimed over the full 5–20 N load range, but the proposed experiment tests only 10 N and therefore cannot evaluate the stated load boundary.
